evidence.quote: my colleagues and I on the FOMC decided last week to maintain our highly accommodative stance of monetary policy
it now appears that real gross domestic product may increase close to or even above the higher end of that range. This annual increase would be the largest in 36 years.
Although I expect these upward price pressures to ease after the temporary supply bottlenecks are resolved, the exact timing of that dynamic is uncertain.
At this point, the risk that inflation remains persistently above our long-run target of 2 percent still appears small.
We are making good progress toward our full employment goal, but we still have a long way to go, and risks remain.
I think we are currently on a good path, and our policy is in a good place.

parsed.rationale: The speaker is upbeat on growth and acknowledges inflation pressures and a willingness to revise her view, which leans hawkish relative to peers. Against that, she endorses the current highly accommodative policy, stresses the employment shortfall, and sees persistent inflation as unlikely, so the net signal is roughly neutral with a slight dovish tilt.
